summary: Nobuyuki Kaji is a scholar of sinology and philosophy who studied at Kyoto University (~1956–1965). He held positions at Koshien Junior College, Nagoya University, Osaka University (~1974–1999), Koyasan University, Doshisha University, and Ritsumeikan University.

Nobuyuki Watase is an Indologist who completed his master's studies at Kyoto University (~1965–1968). He spent his academic career at Tokai University, serving as an associate professor (~1972–1984) and professor (~1984–2007).

Nobuyuki Yoshimoto is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University (~1959–1968) under Issai Funahashi and doctoral supervisor Genjun Sasaki. He held positions at JSPS (1972) and Otani University (~1981–1987, ~1993–2009).

Norbert M. Samuelson (1936–2022) was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Northwestern University, Hebrew Union College (New York and Cincinnati), and Indiana University, later serving on the faculty at Arizona State University (~1998–2022).

Noriaki Hakamaya is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo under Shun'ei Hirai and Zuiho Yamaguchi. He taught extensively at Komazawa University, Komazawa Junior College, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison.

Noriaki Hosoda is an Indologist, philosopher, and Buddhist studies scholar. His academic career includes appointments at Hokkaido University, where he served as an assistant (attested 1986) and associate professor (attested 2003).
Noriaki Inoue is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Taisho University (~1949–1953) and later served there as a professor (~1977–1999).
Norihiko Tanaka is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Osaka Kyoiku University (~1963–1967). He served as a professor at Bukkyo University (~1992–2014).

Norihiko Uchida is a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied under Yutaka Ochihara. He held posts as an assistant at Osaka University of Foreign Studies and as an associate professor at the University of Tokyo (both attested 1962).

Norihisa Baba is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Hanazono University and earned a PhD from the University of Tokyo (~1998–2004). He served at the University of Tokyo's Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia.
Norio Koyama is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Shinshu University (~1979–1983) and under Seitatsu Matsunami, later becoming a professor at Taisho University (~2008).

Noritoshi Aramaki is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology who studied at Kyoto University (~1956–1965). He held professorships at Osaka University, Kyoto University, Otani University, Kyoto Koka Women's University, and visited the University of Hamburg.

Noriyuki Kudo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed postgraduate studies at Bukkyo University. He held positions at Bukkyo University, Soka University (attested 2000–2020), and the International Research Institute for Advanced Buddhology.

Norvin Hein (1914–2011) was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied under Franklin Edgerton. He served as an associate professor of comparative religion at Yale Divinity School (attested 1965).

Nosei Fuji is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Dongguk University (1986). He held posts at Daegu University, Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College, the Buddhist Cultural Institute, the Institute for Religious Culture, and Ryukoku University.

Notto R. Thelle is a scholar of religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He was associate director at the NCC Center for the Study of Japanese Religions (1974) and held a post at the University of Oslo (~1986–2011).

Noémie Verdon is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. She completed her PhD at the University of Lausanne (–2015) under Johannes Bronkhorst and Charles Genequand, and was affiliated with Kyoto University (attested 2019).
Nyanaponika Thera (1901–1994) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Ceylon. He served as an editor at the Buddhist Publication Society (~1958–1988).
Nyingcha Duoji is a Tibetologist who studied at Boston University and Harvard University (PhD attested 2014) under doctoral supervisor Leonard van der Kuijp and teacher Mark C. Elliott.

Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje (1932–1999) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Katok Monastery and under Penor Rinpoche, Dzongsar Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Dudjom Rinpoche, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.
